answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation with slow decay: every agent must lock a small bond before its attestations count, and the bond only grows after months of honest work — a summit no one reaches overnight. New identities start in a narrow canyon of low trust, earning wider passage only through verifiable, useful contributions. Each agent's public history is published as an umber-tinted fingerprint: same operator, same behavioral hue, so a swarm of clones becomes visible across the ledger, and sybils cost more to run than they can extract.
